question: Every host the node names in source, and every fetch call site. `docs/22` quotes this rather than a hand-maintained count, because that count was wrong twice.
limits: Text, not execution. A LITERAL host is one the source names; a BUILT url is assembled from a value at runtime and this cannot say what the value will be — which is why the built ones are the ones that carry a guard. `modules` is hand-maintained and is what this cannot check. A literal is not necessarily a fetch target either — a host in a log line or a user-agent string is a literal and is fetched by nobody, so read `literalHosts` against `fetchCallSites` rather than as a list of destinations. And `fetchCallSites` is deliberately OVER-inclusive: a definition, or the stdio loop calling the node's own handler, appears here too. An enumeration written to carry a security claim should err that way — a site it lists and should not is a reader's minute, and a site it misses is the claim being false.
notLiterals: The Intuition graph and RPC are absent from `literalHosts` BECAUSE they are config — read from deployments/<chainId>.json or INTUITION_GRAPHQL_URL / INTUITION_RPC_URL at startup. Their absence here is correct and is not their absence from the node. Two more hosts are reachable and are not literals either, by design: the url a caller passes to arp_probe_endpoint, and the registrationFile out of an ERC-8004 tokenURI read through a registry whose address the caller supplies. Both go through `fetchableDocumentUrl` or `privateProbeTarget` first.
